newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Newtelco picks international partners.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Newtelco picks international partners.

text.p: New Swiss telecommunications group Newtelco said it had chosen Tele Danmark (TDK) and British Telecom (BT) as its international strategic partners.
"The TDK/BT consortium will acquire a significant minority stake in Newtelco, with the Swiss owners retaining the majority," a Newtelco statement said.

Newtelco was founded in early 1996 as a national operator in the country's deregulating telecommunications market by a Swiss consortium including Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), the biggest Swiss bank.

The other partners are the Swiss Federal Railways (SBB), whose national fibre-optic cable network is the backbone of Newtelco's telecoms network, and the retail federation Migros that dominates the Swiss retail market.
Newtelco said an initial agreement had been signed with the international partners.
It said the agreed terms, which were still subject to final negotiations and due diligence, were not being disclosed.
"TDK and BT both plan to commit extensive resources to Newtelco's future development and to the Swiss market," it said.
Newtelco said both TDK and BT, as successful operators in their liberalised home markets and internationally, would bring the Swiss group experience in competing as an alternative operator.

Newtelco plans to bid for the first Swiss mobile telcommunications license to be offered for private operators in early 1998, when state-owned Telecom PTT loses its mobile business monopoly under a liberalisation package.
Newtelco began offering broad band data services to business customers in November and has won several orders, including from internet provider Swiss Online.
It says intends to expand to a full range of data, voice and multimedia services.

Switzerland's lower house of parliament approved a liberalisation package this week that would lift Telecom PTT's monopoly over most voice transmission and the cellular phone network in 1998, when the EU liberalises its communications market.
The bill must still be approved by the upper house.

Besides Telecom PTT, Newtelco will also be competing against DIAX, a telecoms group formed this year by six Swiss power utilities who have chosen SBC Communications Inc. of the U.S. as an alliance partner.

Efforts to liberalise the Swiss telecommunications market have been under way for several years and a first step was taken in 1991 when Switzerland allowed private companies to offer some kinds of data transmission.
